The answer's claims are mostly supported. The SchNet passage says the C20 reference data came from DFT at the PBE level with the TS van der Waals correction, and that SchNet was trained at the PBE+vdW-TS level. The DiffTRe passage supports the obstacle (limited availability of precise, broad data sets) and the point that quantum mechanics computations for macromolecules stay intractable and prevent ab initio data set generation. It also supports the DimeNet++ diamond case (experimental stiffness tensor) and the coarse-grained water case (pressure, radial and angular distribution functions).

One claim needs a closer look: "DiffTRe takes a top-down approach and trains neural network potentials on experimental data." The passage supports this, since it contrasts top-down approaches with bottom-up learning and says DiffTRe addresses the call for NN potentials trained on experimental data.
